newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai stocks support fund to give cheap loans.
newsitem.headline: New Thai stocks support fund to give cheap loans.

text.p: A new 10-billion-baht (US$400 million) support fund set up by the Thai governnment to shore up the depressed stock market will lend funds at a concessional rate to cash-strapped investors, a brokers' representative said.

Viroj Nualkhae, chairman of Phatra Thanakit Plc, who was at a meeting with government officials to map out the fund's workings, said on Thursday the fund would charge small investors a lending rate similar to that given to state enterprises from next Monday.
Investors tapping the support fund to be run by the Government Savings Bank would be required to put up shares as collateral, he told reporters.
The mortgaged shares must be redeemed from the bank within two years or even sooner if the market recovers from its current extended slump.
The new support fund is the latest initiative in a joint government and private sector attempt to reverse a slide in the Thai bourse to three-year-lows.
Forced selling by brokerages of shares held by investors unable to top up their margin calls has been depressing shares.
Another 15.27 billion baht rescue fund that was launched in August by bankers and brokers has been in the stock market since last Friday to prop up prices.
The SET index was up 6.09 points at 1002.25 when the market closed for lunch on Thursday. Brokers attributed the positive tone to news about the new fund and buying by the other private sector fund.
Bunyarak Ningsanond, president of the Government Savings Bank, said investors qualifying to borrow from the fund would largely be those trying to avoid having shares force-sold.
He said the government decision should reduce cases of forced share sales by investors since the composite SET index has fallen more than 20 percent since July 1.
Viroj said the government-owned bank would accept, as collateral, both blue-chip and other listed stocks with a fair earnings record.
He said the bank was prepared to enlarge the fund to 50 billion baht which would be sufficient to offset the volume of impending forced share sales estimated at 5.0 billion baht.
